# Next-Gen Packaging Materials Discussion

Date: 2023-08-02  
Attendees: Saskia Fennmoor, Tobiah Ulmford  

### Agenda  
- Review performance of current insulation materials  
- Evaluate new composite samples for extended cold-chain duration  
- Discuss cost implications and integration challenges  

### Discussion  
Saskia presented data on the existing foam-based insulation, noting reliable temperature maintenance for up to 48 hours but degradation beyond 60 hours in high-humidity conditions. Tobiah introduced three new composite materials sourced from Lumitech Labs showing potential for 72-hour temperature stability at -20°C. Sample #2, a multi-layer aerogel hybrid composite, demonstrated a 30% improvement in thermal retention over current standards during tests in the Windmere warehouse. However, its cost is approximately 18% higher per unit volume. Integration concerns were raised regarding sensor tag compatibility due to material density differing from current foam packaging. Tobiah suggested a pilot run using the #2 composite on select vaccine shipments in September 2023 to gather real-world data.  

### Decisions  
- Proceed with limited pilot deployment of composite #2 in September  
- Maintain current foam insulation for shipments under 48 hours  
- Initiate cost-benefit analysis to be completed by 2023-09-20  

### Action Items  
- Tobiah: Coordinate pilot logistics and sensor tag calibration by 2023-08-15  
- Saskia: Prepare cost-benefit analysis framework by 2023-08-10  
- Both: Schedule follow-up review meeting for 2023-09-25
